source_text: Ad quid ergo persuadendum aut Scripturas releges, aut conscios nominabis, qui adhuc quod sentis non potes definire? Quid te iuvat, ut Adam doceas deliquisse, quod ego penitus non refello? Quaerimus, Adam ante tot saecula mortuo, peccatum, quo in diaboli ius Dei imago transcribitur, per quid inveniatur in parvulo.
pass_a_gloss: To persuading what, therefore, will you either reread the Scriptures, or name those in the know, you who still cannot define what you mean? What helps you, that you teach that Adam offended, which I do not refute inwardly at all? We ask, Adam having died so many ages ago, through what the sin, by which the image of God is transcribed into the devil's right, is found in a little child.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS parvulus; Blaise infants in original-sin debate

pass_b_english: What, then, will you try to persuade us of by rereading Scripture or naming people who agree with you, when you still cannot define your own view? What good does it do you to prove that Adam sinned, something I do not deny at all? Adam died so many centuries ago. Our question is through what sin is found in an infant—the sin by which God’s image is transferred to the devil’s ownership.

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
Augustine's quoted claim that the unbaptized remain under the devil; keep the personal devil, not 'evil'.
rejected: under Satan (name not in the Latin here)

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
